# Source Comparability Disclosure

Last updated: 2026-05-13

This disclosure is written for external readers of the atlas and release
dataset. It explains where the project inputs are directly comparable, where
they are only comparable within a source family, and where the project uses
labelled extension sources rather than the core baseline source stack.

This note records whether the project's core inputs are comparable enough to
support the published LI, ILI, HLI, and IHLI indicators. It focuses on
measurement characteristics that can change interpretation even when formulas
are implemented correctly: monetary units, price-year treatment, inequality
concepts, health-expectancy definitions, and observed versus modelled evidence.

The short conclusion is:

- National `LI` and `HLI` monetary inputs are on the strongest footing because
  national `GDPpc` uses World Bank WDI `NY.GDP.PCAP.PP.KD`, which is GDP per
  capita in constant 2021 international dollars adjusted by purchasing power
  parity.
- Subnational monetary inputs are not all the same currency/price-family. EU
  NUTS2 uses Eurostat PPS, OECD regional layers use OECD regional PPP-style units, China
  uses NBS/GDL source-family inputs, Mexico currently uses a GDL income proxy,
  Argentina uses constant-2004-peso PBG per capita, and Sri Lanka uses nominal
  monthly household income.
- Gini inputs are numerically standardized to 0-1, but their survey concepts
  differ. This is why the project keeps `Core baseline`, `Extended Gini`, and
  regional-source provenance separate.
- WHO HALE and IHME/GBD HALE should not be described as the same evidence class.
  WHO GHO remains the core baseline HALE source; IHME/GBD is accepted as a
  clearly labelled modelled extension.

# Current Formula Implications

The indicators inherit the measurement unit of the component inputs.

| indicator | formula | inherited unit issue |
|---|---|---|
| `LI` | `GDPpc * LEXP` | Monetary unit of `GDPpc` multiplied by years of life expectancy. |
| `ILI` | `GDPpc * LEXP * (1 - Gini)` | Same monetary-life unit as `LI`, adjusted by a unitless inequality factor. |
| `HLI` | `GDPpc * HALE` | Monetary unit of `GDPpc` multiplied by healthy-life-expectancy years. |
| `IHLI` | `GDPpc * HALE * (1 - Gini)` | Same monetary-healthy-life unit as `HLI`, adjusted by a unitless inequality factor. |

This means inflation and purchasing-power treatment matter most for `GDPpc`.
If a GDPpc input is current-price or local-currency, `LI` and `HLI` can be
distorted by inflation or exchange-rate changes. If a GDPpc input is constant
PPP, it is much better suited for comparisons over time and across countries.

# National Source Comparability

## GDPpc

Current national input:

- Pipeline artifact: `data/raw/downloads/gdppc_ppp_constant_1990_2024_all.csv`
- Pipeline source code: `scripts/bootstrap_worldbank_inputs.sh`
- WDI code: `NY.GDP.PCAP.PP.KD`
- World Bank label in the downloaded artifact: `GDP per capita, PPP (constant 2021 international $)`
- Source link: <https://databank.worldbank.org/metadataglossary/world-development-indicators/series/NY.GDP.PCAP.PP.KD>

Decision:

- Treat the national monetary spine as inflation-adjusted and PPP-adjusted.
- Interpret national `LI`, `ILI`, `HLI`, and `IHLI` as using constant 2021
  international-dollar GDPpc units.
- Do not mix national values with subnational values from other monetary
  source-families without an explicit comparability warning.

Remaining caveat:

- A change in World Bank PPP benchmark year can revise historical levels. The
  project should keep the WDI code and downloaded file headers in the release
  dataset so users can see which benchmark was used.

## LEXP

Current national input:

- Pipeline artifact: `data/raw/downloads/lexp_1990_2024_all.csv`
- WDI code: `SP.DYN.LE00.IN`
- World Bank label in the downloaded artifact: `Life expectancy at birth, total (years)`
- Source link: <https://databank.worldbank.org/metadataglossary/world-development-indicators/series/SP.DYN.LE00.IN>

Decision:

- Treat national `LEXP` as life expectancy at birth, total population.
- It is conceptually aligned with the paper formula and with the current website
  labels.

Remaining caveat:

- Life expectancy is a period life-table measure, not a forecast of a real
  newborn cohort. This is standard and should not be treated as a project flaw,
  but the Methods page should keep "at birth" language clear.

## Gini

Current core national input:

- Pipeline artifact: `data/raw/downloads/gini_1990_2024_all.csv`
- WDI code: `SI.POV.GINI`
- World Bank label in the downloaded artifact: `Gini index`
- Source link: <https://databank.worldbank.org/metadataglossary/world-development-indicators/series/SI.POV.GINI>

Decision:

- Treat World Bank WDI Gini as the core baseline inequality input.
- Normalize all Gini values to the 0-1 scale before applying `(1 - Gini)`.
- Keep the World Bank caveat visible: WDI Gini can be based on income or, in
  some countries, consumption expenditure.

Remaining caveat:

- Gini values are unitless but not automatically concept-identical. Income
  Gini, consumption Gini, disposable-income Gini, equivalised-household-income
  Gini, and modelled disposable-income Gini can differ materially.

## HALE

Current core national input:

- Pipeline artifact: `data/raw/downloads/hale_who_1990_2024_all.csv`
- WHO GHO indicator: `WHOSIS_000002`
- Pipeline filter: `Dim1=SEX_BTSX` and `SpatialDimType=COUNTRY`
- Source link: <https://www.who.int/data/gho/data/indicators/indicator-details/GHO/gho-ghe-hale-healthy-life-expectancy-at-birth>
- WHO metadata link: <https://www.who.int/data/gho/indicator-metadata-registry/imr-details/7752>

Decision:

- Treat WHO GHO HALE as the core baseline HALE source.
- Treat it as healthy life expectancy at birth, both sexes, in years.
- Preserve the split publication policy: core HLI/IHLI cannot extend past the
  available WHO HALE years without an explicit extension source.

Remaining caveat:

- WHO HALE is an estimated summary measure and is not the same as raw observed
  mortality. WHO metadata notes method revisions over time; cross-release
  comparisons should therefore keep the downloaded artifact date and indicator
  code visible.

# Extended National Tracks

## Extended Gini

Current implementation:

- Source fusion script: `scripts/fuse_gini_sources.py`
- Stage B runner: `scripts/run_stage_b_multisource_extension.sh`
- Rule: first non-null source by explicit priority.
- Typical source concepts in the runner:
  - `wb_income_or_consumption`
  - `wiid_disposable_income`
  - `wid_disposable_income`
  - `oecd_idd_disposable_income`
  - `swiid_disposable_income`

Decision:

- Extended Gini improves computability, not conceptual purity.
- The extension is acceptable because it is separated from the core baseline and
  because row-level source labels are kept in details/audit files.
- The website and release dataset must not describe Extended Gini as if every
  row used one identical survey concept.

Recommended website wording:

> Extended Gini adds additional inequality sources where the core World Bank
> Gini is missing; source concepts can differ and are carried in provenance
> fields.

## Extended Gini + Extended HALE

Current implementation:

- Builder: `scripts/build_ihme_national_hale_track_v2.py`
- Source bundle: `ihme_gbd_2023_national_hale_modelled`
- Quality label: `ihme_modelled_hale_age_id_22_all_ages_metric_years_national`
- Source link: <https://vizhub.healthdata.org/gbd-results/>

Decision:

- IHME/GBD HALE is accepted as a modelled HALE extension, not as a replacement
  for WHO GHO HALE.
- It belongs in the `Extended Gini + Extended HALE` track.
- It should improve coverage only where the conservative WB ISO3 to IHME bridge
  maps unambiguously.

Remaining caveat:

- The current IHME export is labelled `age_id 22 / All Ages`, sex Both, metric
  Years. IHME publications report HALE as a life-expectancy-at-birth summary measure, while the Results Tool export labels the age field as `All Ages`. The project therefore describes this as IHME/GBD modelled HALE, exported with age `All Ages` and interpreted as HALE at birth following GBD reporting conventions; the exact source label remains visible.

# Subnational Source Comparability

Subnational outputs should be interpreted as source-family regional evidence,
not as one perfectly harmonized global regional panel.

| source family | current use | monetary or concept note | interpretation decision |
|---|---|---|---|
| Eurostat NUTS2 | EU27 NUTS2 `LI`; Portugal, Spain, France, Poland, Austria `ILI` overlays | GDP per inhabitant is `PPS_EU27_2020_HAB`; life expectancy is Eurostat regional life expectancy at birth. | Strong within-EU regional lane; not a literal replacement for World Bank constant 2021 international dollars. |
| OECD regional layers | U.S., Canada, Germany, China/India OECD-style regional layers where present | OECD regional GDPpc uses OECD regional PPP-style units in the probe files. | Useful for OECD-family regional comparison; keep source-family labels. |
| Statistics Canada | Canada Gini and other provincial inputs | After-tax Gini and official Canadian regional tables. | Good national-statistical-office source; concept differs from ACS, EU-SILC, and WDI Gini. |
| U.S. Census ACS | U.S. state Gini | ACS B19083 state Gini. | Good U.S. source; not identical to EU-SILC disposable/equivalised concepts. |
| NBS China + GDL | China province LI layer | NBS provincial GDPpc plus GDL life expectancy or paper-comparison inputs, depending on lane. | Formula-compatible but not yet a full paper replication or ILI output without province Gini. |
| GDL + INEGI Mexico | Mexico state `LI`/`ILI` layer | GDL `lgnic` is an income/GNI-style proxy, not official state GDPpc; ENIGH supplies Gini. | Useful labelled regional layer; should not be described as official state GDPpc-based ILI. |
| Argentina DNAP | Argentina province/CABA `LI`/`ILI` layer | PBG per capita is in constant 2004 Argentine pesos; LEXP is a male/female average; Gini is EPH Total Urbano household per-capita family-income Gini. | Useful within-Argentina regional layer; not directly comparable in levels to PPP GDPpc lanes. |
| Sri Lanka DCS | Sri Lanka district `LI`/`ILI` layer | Income is nominal monthly household income in Sri Lankan rupees; LEXP is 2011-2013 male/female average; Gini is 2019 household-income Gini. | Useful within-Sri-Lanka district layer; not directly comparable in levels to PPP GDPpc lanes and should be read with the time-shifted LEXP caveat. |
| IHME/GBD subnational HALE | selected regional HLI/IHLI | Modelled HALE joined through curated bridges. | Allowed as labelled modelled extension only. |

Important consequence:

- It is acceptable to compare regions within a regional dataset, and often within a
  common source family such as EU NUTS2.
- It is not yet methodologically clean to rank every subnational region in the
  world as if all GDPpc and Gini concepts were identical.

# Geography Bridge Disclosure

The atlas distinguishes a missing source from a geography mismatch. A source is
not discarded merely because its region names or boundary level differ from the
current atlas layer, but it is also not used unless the bridge can be explained
and reproduced.

The project currently allows these geography bridges:

- Exact region-code joins, such as NUTS2 IDs or official province/district
  codes.
- Name or alias joins where the regions are the same but labels differ because
  of spelling, language, abbreviations, or diacritics.
- Aggregation from smaller source units to a broader displayed region, ideally
  with weights when the source concept requires them.
- Assignment from a broader but still genuinely subnational source region to
  its documented component regions, with a visible geography-proxy label.
- Separate source-specific geography layers when a useful source does not match
  an existing atlas geography.

The project does not allow national-to-regional fanout in the main subnational
atlas. A national Gini, national HALE, or national life expectancy value is not
copied to all provinces, states, districts, or regions simply to fill gaps. If a
future sensitivity exercise uses national values this way, it must be released
as a separate experimental approximation product rather than as observed or
modelled subnational evidence.

Examples:

- Saudi Arabia is mapped through five genuine GDL macro-regions built from
  documented component administrative regions. This is a grouped subnational
  bridge, not national fanout.
- Thailand uses province-level HALE and province-level income Gini grouped to
  five GDL macro-regions. The Gini bridge is an unweighted province mean and is
  therefore labelled as a grouped subnational proxy, not a recomputed
  macro-region distribution.
- Belgium uses Sciensano healthy life years at age 15 as a labelled HLE proxy,
  not at-birth HALE. Flanders and Wallonia are broader source regions assigned
  to component NUTS2 provinces, while Brussels is exact.
- France and Spain include labelled cases where a broader or combined regional
  source value is assigned to component NUTS2 rows because the source reports a
  real subnational combined unit.
- Argentina and Sri Lanka use region-code joins for the implemented province
  and district datasets.
- Broad GDL SHDI regional datasets remain their own geography layers when they
  do not match another atlas source family.

# Specific Risks And Current Mitigations

## Risk 1: inflation or price-year mismatch in lifetime income

Assessment:

- National tracks: handled well by World Bank constant 2021 PPP GDPpc.
- EU NUTS2: handled within Eurostat PPS source-family, but not the same unit as
  World Bank constant 2021 international dollars.
- Mexico GDL: not official GDPpc; it is an income proxy.
- China and other regional layers: source-family notes remain necessary.

Mitigation:

- Keep national and subnational comparability caveats visible.
- Add a Methods note that `LI` values inherit the GDPpc source unit.
- Preserve source bundle, method flag, and quality flag columns in downloads.

## Risk 2: Gini concept mismatch

Assessment:

- Numerically standardized: yes.
- Conceptually harmonized across all sources: no.

Mitigation:

- Keep `Core baseline` and `Extended Gini` separate.
- Keep subnational overlay source labels visible.
- Avoid describing Extended Gini as an official harmonized inequality panel.
- Germany and Netherlands now add official observed regional Gini overlays, but
  their concepts remain source-specific: Germany uses the Statistikportal
  Mikrozensus Land income-distribution Gini, while the Netherlands uses CBS VSO
  province Gini for standardized disposable income of private households
  excluding student households. Germany NUTS2 rows using broader Land values are
  labelled as geography proxies.

## Risk 3: HALE source and age-definition confusion

Assessment:

- WHO GHO core HALE is clearly HALE at birth.
- IHME/GBD HALE is modelled and labelled with GBD export fields.
- OWID is not currently a production replacement; it is a validation mirror for
  WHO HALE.

Mitigation:

- Keep WHO HALE in the core baseline.
- Keep IHME/GBD HALE only in the labelled Extended HALE lane.
- On the website, say "modelled IHME/GBD HALE" rather than simply "extra HALE."

# Website Disclosure Decision

The website should include a short Methods panel with these points:

1. National LI/HLI use World Bank constant 2021 PPP GDPpc, so national monetary
   comparisons are inflation- and purchasing-power-adjusted.
2. Regional LI/HLI inherit the monetary unit of their source family; EU
   NUTS2, OECD TL2, GDL, NBS, and national-stat-office lanes are source-family
   comparable, not one globally harmonized regional currency panel.
3. Gini values are scaled consistently, but source concepts differ. Extended
   Gini and subnational overlays therefore remain labelled.
4. WHO HALE is the core baseline health input; IHME/GBD HALE is a clearly
   labelled modelled extension.
